name: Serdev suture

lead: The Serdev suture is a thread-lift technique in which sutures are placed under the skin to hold sagging tissue up, rather than cutting skin out. It is associated with a surgeon named Serdev and belongs to the suspension-thread family of minimally invasive lifts.

Suture threads placed in the dermis and subcutis anchor lax tissue in a higher position for a tighter-looking face. A 2016 review of suspension threads notes that Serdev introduced a polycaproamide suture; published evidence on this specific needle method is thin.

paras: It is done by a trained practitioner as an in-office or minor-surgery procedure, as a lower-downtime alternative to a facelift. Results are visible once placed.
The 2016 review reports that early sutures increased inflammatory reaction. General references note that threads can be difficult to remove and that practitioner training varies.

angle.text: People want a tighter, lifted face without a full facelift. Needle sutures anchor sagging facial tissue in a higher position, and the lift is visible when placed. Published evidence on this specific technique is thin.

lead: The Serdev suture is a needle-based suture lifting technique for facial rejuvenation, associated with a surgeon named Serdev, who introduced a polycaproamide suture for facial lifting. It belongs to the broader family of suspension or thread lifts [1][2].

A 2016 review of suspension threads states that Sulamanidze and colleagues began using polypropylene threads after Serdev introduced a suture made of polycaproamide, and that these early sutures increased inflammatory reaction [1]. Thread lifts are described in general references as non-surgical alternatives to facelifts, with some safety concerns about variable practitioner training [2].

paras: Suture threads are described as a minimally invasive technique for facial rejuvenation that uses absorbable and non-absorbable sutures placed in the dermis and subcutis to lift lax tissue, with fewer incisions and shorter recovery than conventional facelifts [1]. Wikipedia describes thread lifts as a non-surgical facelift in which barbed threads pull the skin of the face and neck upward without skin excision [2].
The sources available for this entry do not describe the specifics of the Serdev needle technique or its modern variants.

The 2016 review notes that early sutures increased inflammatory reaction [1]. Wikipedia reports a cosmetic doctor describing thread lifts as potentially the most dangerous procedure an aesthetic practitioner can perform because threads may stay in the skin and cannot easily be removed, and cites a BBC investigation that found short training courses and poor infection control in an undercover course in the UK [2].
No studies found. A 2016 narrative review of suspension threads in general, covering several suture types, is available [1].
